description:
What If Earth Suddenly Stopped Spinning?

At the equator you are moving at about 1,670 km/h. If Earth stopped spinning, everything not attached to bedrock would keep going.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#earth #whatif #space #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: What would happen to you if Earth suddenly stopped spinning?
Right now, if you're near the equator, you're moving at about one thousand six hundred and seventy kilometers per hour.
You don't feel it, because everything around you is moving too. The air, the oceans, the buildings.
segments.headline: You don't feel it

segments.text: If the ground stopped, all of that would keep going. Winds faster than any hurricane would sweep the planet.

visual.query: ISS-20 Thunderstorms on the Brazilian Horizon
commons: ISS-20 Thunderstorms on the Brazilian Horizon

segments.headline: Winds beyond any hurricane

segments.text: Oceans would surge across the land.

visual.query: ISS-45 StoryOfWater, Great Barrier Reef, Australia
commons: ISS-45 StoryOfWater, Great Barrier Reef, Australia

segments.headline: Oceans on the move

segments.text: And once things calmed down, one day would last a whole year: six months of daylight, then six months of night.
Good news: Earth isn't going to stop. It's slowing, but only by milliseconds per century.
segments.headline: Don't worry
